notes: Copilot's multi-agent orchestration feature is /fleet, which the vendor defines as 'parallel subagent execution' (api.schema.json UIExitPlanModeAction.autopilot_fleet) over the SAME in-process subagents scenario 3.1 uses: N concurrent subagent.started lines land in the parent's own events.jsonl, keyed by a per-call toolCallId, and no child session-state/<id>/ directory is ever created. Four of the seven canonical claudecode phases are therefore UNREACHABLE here by agent architecture, not by defect — child_session_birth (transcript_new), parent_linked, the per-child working→ready drain, and children_swept (transcript_removed) — and the 'no journal / no unknown-project phantom session' guard is vacuous because copilot writes no per-run directory or bookkeeping file at all. What this spec CAN assert is the parent arc: ready→working on the fan-out prompt, HELD working across all three children (both subagent events are Skip=true, parser.go:390, and copilot's only turn boundary is the explicit assistant.turn_end), and working→ready only after the last child returns. That arc is correct today, so this cell is NOT known_failing. NOT ASSERTABLE HERE, and the reason this spec looks thinner than the scenario: SubagentCount(parent)=N. The daemon does compute it — the parser's toolCallId-keyed openSubagents set survives concurrency, countOpenSubagents now reads the LIVE parser (metrics/adapter.go:106-163, the #1256 seam fix), and ComputeSubagentSummary (grouped.go:266-300) makes Total=Working=OpenSubagents with no file children — but expected.jsonl's DSL has no subagent-count predicate AND the daemon's recorded events.jsonl carries no metrics vector at all (its keys are only adapter/cwd/file_size/hook_name/kind/new_state/parent_session_id/pid/prev_state/project_dir/reason/seq/session_id/transcript_path/ts). The N-concurrency proof lives in the recipe's verify as a gate over the AGENT store: at least two (target three) subagent.started unmatched at once, and every subagent.completed BEFORE the first assistant.turn_end — the second condition is the mirror image of the 3.2 gate and is what distinguishes this SYNC fan-out from the background case whose held-working defect this cell deliberately does not touch. Single-birth adapter (agent.FilesUnderRoot + sessionIDFromPath key the session to its session-state/<id>/ dir), so the birth is one phase anchored to start UNPINNED. duration_at_least_ms on the working phase bounds the held-working window: 15000ms is a floor chosen well under the recipe's three concurrent `sleep 25` children, not the span itself. model is left unpinned (--model accepts only "auto"; the parent's effective model is resolved at runtime via session.auto_mode_resolved, and the children run claude-haiku-4.5 independently) and cost is unasserted — record fills both from the recording.
source: workflow-fanout scenario (issue #565) → copilot /fleet-style parallel subagent fan-out

text: The copilot session appears in ready once session-state/<id>/events.jsonl is written

The fan-out prompt drives the session ready → working as the workflow starts, and it STAYS working across the whole concurrent fan-out — it neither settles to ready nor drops into waiting while the three children run. SubagentCount(parent) tracks the live child count over this window (OpenSubagents → ComputeSubagentSummary; not expressible as a phase, gated in the recipe's verify). --allow-all pre-approves every tool, so no permission.requested is written and waiting must never appear.

Only after the last child returns does the parent's explicit assistant.turn_end fire: working → ready. Because the fan-out is SYNC (parallel tool calls block the turn), this transition necessarily lands after every subagent.completed — and SubagentCount(parent) is back to 0, the set having emptied as each toolCallId was matched.
